thread:
marisa: quick thought — what if instead of sending full eviction intents per-prefix we send compact delta tokens that the sequencer can coalesce? reduces RPCs and should smooth tail latency.
cheng: can you sketch the delta format? curious about correctness during concurrent demotes.
dan: so like send (+n) or (-n) counters per prefix id? my worry: ordering hazards across rebinds.
marisa: exactly, lightweight shape: `PREFIX_DELTA := {prefix_id: int, delta: int, epoch: uint64}`. sequencer keeps monotonic epoch per prefix and applies deltas in order it sees epochs.
olivia: hmm epoch solves reordering but what about retries and idempotency? if a delta is applied twice we could overshoot.
marisa: include op-id hash for dedup at sequencer; sequencer stores small recent op-id cache per prefix.
sam: dedup cache per prefix might blow memory for hot prefixes though.
cheng: we can make it bounded with LRU + probabilistic Bloom filter for recent op-ids. false positives harmless (they drop a legitimate delta) — but that affects correctness.
dan: dropping a delta is not harmless — it changes residency counts. we need deterministic repair.
marisa: good point. proposal: sequencer tracks applied-opcount + checkpoint snapshots every X seconds; if Bloom filter false-positive leads to missed application the periodic checkpoint will reconcile via full intent reconciliation path.
olivia: reconciliation path is heavy. can we instead make deltas commutative and ensure monotonicity so replay twice doesn't break invariants?
marisa: deltas are commutative on counts, but replay double increments. if we make delta represent absolute target (set-to) with epoch it's safer but more traffic.
sam: absolute set-to means more churn on hot prefixes because every small change sends a new absolute.
cheng: tradeoff: compact deltas + probabilistic dedup + reconciliation window vs absolute updates with higher bandwidth. which is better for multi-tenant shared pools?
dan: also need to consider handoff: when prefix ownership moves, sequencer must forward outstanding deltas or tombstone them.
marisa: interface boundary: runtime (allocator) proposes delta ops to sequencer via new RPC `ApplyPrefixDelta(prefDelta)`. sequencer guarantees at-least-once delivery to prefix owner node(s). ownership transfer requires sequencer to encode transfer epoch so new owner can ignore older epoch deltas.
olivia: add API `TransferFence(prefix, new_owner, transfer_epoch)` so sequencer can pause delta application while transfer finalizes.
sam: ops question: how do we observe correctness? metrics to add: delta-apply-latency, dedup-filter-false-positives, reconciliation-rate, prefix-count-drift.
cheng: can we simulate workload with trace playback? I can run a synthetic with hot-key churn and measure drift under Bloom rates.
marisa: yes please. also need a canary mode: fallback to legacy full-intent RPC if delta path reports anomalies above threshold. config flag per-node.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout plan created: canary-group=eviction-deltas-small, 5% traffic for 4h, alert if drift > 0.5% or reconciliation-rate > 0.1%.
dan: what about cross-region failover? deltas must survive inter-region rebinds; use durable sequencing log and transfer_epoch semantics.
olivia: plus ensure read-after-write: when a client pins then immediately reads, it must see the effect. we need sync point: pin completion should await sequencer ack for delta application or read from owner shard.
marisa: agreed. pin API semantics: return success only after delta ack from sequencer. we can offer async pin with eventual visibility for non-critical paths.
sam: one more: telemetry tagging for tombstones and transfer events so we can correlate with hot-prefix regressions.
marisa: next steps: cheng to prototype Bloom + dedup + reconciliation in sim, dan to sketch `ApplyPrefixDelta` + `TransferFence` RPCs and invariants, olivia to draft canary + alerting runbook, i'll write a one-pager RFC follow-up with tradeoffs.
cheng: will do sim and post results in a follow-up thread.
dan: i'll sketch RPCs and e2e invariants by EOD tomorrow.
marisa: great — thanks. feel free to @marisa if you hit blockers.
infra-bot: reminder: thread archived after 30 days if no activity.
